business_health.title: BUSINESS HEALTH ASSESSMENT GUIDE
business_health.overview: Dimension 1: Assess the strategic value and operational health of business capabilities — independent of technology

dimensions.name: STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE
dimensions.question: How critical is this capability to BCI's mission and strategic objectives?

scale.Label: Mission-Critical
scale.Description: Essential to BCI's investment mandate; regulatory/fiduciary requirement; failure severely impacts beneficiaries or operations; no viable alternatives
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Directly enables investment returns, client commitments, or regulatory compliance. Loss triggers immediate escalation.

scale.Label: Important
scale.Description: Contributes meaningfully to operations; supports strategic goals; temporary degradation manageable; standard industry practice
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Necessary for efficient operations but short-term absence wouldn't halt critical functions.

scale.Label: Supporting
scale.Description: Provides convenience or efficiency gains; alternatives readily available; minimal strategic impact if eliminated
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Could be outsourced, eliminated, or significantly reduced without material business impact.

dimensions.name: OPERATIONAL HEALTH
dimensions.question: How healthy is this capability from a risk, compliance, and operational perspective?

scale.Label: Healthy
scale.Description: No significant pain points; low operational risk; meets all compliance requirements; stakeholders satisfied; issues rare
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: No active issues or complaints. Audit/compliance reviews clean. Stakeholders express satisfaction.

scale.Label: Moderate Concerns
scale.Description: Noticeable pain points; moderate risk exposure; some compliance gaps; periodic stakeholder complaints; workarounds needed
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Known issues exist but are managed. Some workarounds required. Moderate audit findings.

scale.Label: Unhealthy
scale.Description: Severe pain points; high risk exposure; compliance violations; frequent complaints; capability barely functioning
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Active escalations, significant audit findings, or risk events. Stakeholders actively dissatisfied.

business_tech_fit.title: BUSINESS-TECHNOLOGY FIT ASSESSMENT GUIDE
business_tech_fit.overview: Dimension 2: Assess how well technology serves the business capability — fit and automation — from the business perspective

dimensions.name: LEVEL OF AUTOMATION
dimensions.question: To what extent does technology automate work vs. requiring manual effort?

scale.Label: Highly Automated
scale.Description: Routine work automated end-to-end; minimal manual intervention; humans focus on exceptions and judgment; scalable without proportional headcount
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Routine tasks automated. Manual effort for exceptions/decisions only. Volume increases don't require proportional staff.

scale.Label: Partially Automated
scale.Description: Mix of automated and manual; some routine tasks still require human effort; automation exists but gaps remain
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Some automation but significant manual steps persist. Efficiency gains possible through further automation.

scale.Label: Mostly Manual
scale.Description: Heavy manual effort; extensive spreadsheet/email work; automation minimal; scaling requires proportional headcount increase
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Most work is manual. Heavy reliance on spreadsheets/email. Growth requires adding people.

dimensions.name: TECHNOLOGY FIT
dimensions.question: Does technology adequately cover and meet the business requirements of this capability?

scale.Label: Excellent Fit
scale.Description: Technology comprehensively covers all capability needs; meets business requirements exceptionally well; enables best practices; users satisfied; no significant gaps
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: All key activities have appropriate tooling. System enables (not constrains) work. Users are satisfied with functionality.

scale.Label: Adequate Fit
scale.Description: Technology covers most needs with some gaps; meets core requirements but workarounds exist; functional but not optimal; mixed user satisfaction
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Core functions covered but notable gaps. Workarounds needed for some activities. Users express mixed satisfaction.

scale.Label: Poor Fit
scale.Description: Technology has major coverage gaps; doesn't meet core business needs; wrong tool for the job; constrains capability; heavy reliance on manual workarounds
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Frequent complaints about missing functionality or coverage gaps. System constrains rather than enables work.

tech_health.title: TECHNOLOGY HEALTH SCORING GUIDE
tech_health.overview: Dimension 3: Assess the technical health and alignment with BCI's technology standards and direction — from the IT perspective

dimensions.name: TECHNOLOGY OPERATIONAL HEALTH
dimensions.question: How healthy is this technology from reliability, supportability, and lifecycle perspectives?

scale.Label: Healthy
scale.Description: Highly reliable; actively supported by vendor; regular updates; modern architecture; well-integrated; no significant technical debt or security concerns
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Reliable, well-supported, receives updates, integrates well with ecosystem.

scale.Label: Moderate Concerns
scale.Description: Generally reliable but some issues; support adequate but not excellent; updates infrequent; aging but functional; some integration friction; manageable technical debt
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Works but has some reliability/support/integration gaps. May be aging but not urgent to replace.

scale.Label: Unhealthy
scale.Description: Frequent reliability issues; limited/no vendor support; no updates; legacy/obsolete; significant technical debt; security vulnerabilities; poorly integrated
scale.Assessment Guidance: Select if: Reliability problems, lacks support, obsolete, has security issues, or creates integration bottlenecks.

dimensions.name: TECHNOLOGY DIRECTION ALIGNMENT
dimensions.question:
How well does this technology align with BCI's technology direction? 
Note: assessment based on alignment with specific tech direction components listed below.

scale.Description: Compliance with enterprise architecture principles, approved technology stack, integration patterns
scale.Assessment Sample Questions: Does it follow EA standards / guidelines? Uses approved platforms?

scale.Description: Alignment with BCI's cloud-first direction; cloud-native, cloud-ready, or cloud-compatible
scale.Assessment Sample Questions: Is it cloud-native? Can it be migrated? SaaS where possible?

scale.Description: Compliance with Zero-Trust architecture principles; identity-centric security; least-privilege access
Readiness to leverage AI/ML capabilities; data accessibility; API availability for AI integration
scale.Assessment Sample Questions: Can AI tools integrate? Data accessible for ML?

scale.Label: Fully Aligned
scale.Description: Assessed technology explicitly aligns with a specific technology direction component.

scale.Label: Partially Aligned
scale.Description: Assessed technology meets some requirements from the specific technology direction component.

scale.Label: Fully Aligned
scale.Description: Aligns with BCI technical standards; supports Cloud strategy; compliant with Zero-Trust security model; AI-enabled or AI-ready; on strategic technology roadmap

scale.Label: Partially Aligned
scale.Description: Meets some technical standards but gaps exist; limited Cloud readiness; partial Zero-Trust compliance; no current AI enablement but not blocking

scale.Label: Misaligned
scale.Description: Conflicts with BCI technical standards; not Cloud-compatible; violates Zero-Trust principles; blocks AI enablement; requires replacement or major remediation
